history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — Buddhist (Theravada) monastery of the Tai-Khamti community; keep-or-drop decision needed. CSV TOWN CORRECTION: Chongkham (also spelt Chowkham) is not in Tezu — it is a historic Tai-Khamti village in Namsai district, about 15-22 km from Namsai town. 'Chongkham' literally means 'golden (kham) temple (chong)'; local tradition says the old monastery had a gold-plated roof and the village grew around it. The original 18th-century temple has been replaced by a newer structure. A Buddhist-conclave report describes Chongkham Raj Vihara as one of the oldest monasteries in the region; an academic survey notes a large stupa built at Chowkham on 10 March 1990 by Chow Khamoon Gohain and a dozen early-20th-century votive stupas around the monastery. Coordinates (27.80782, 96.03689) are from the mapped 'Chongkham Buddhist Temple' location pin at Chowkham — approximate; the exact Raj Vihara plot is not independently verified.

name: Chongkham Raj Vihara (Chongkham Buddhist Temple)
town_description: Chongkham (Chowkham) is a historic Tai-Khamti village in Namsai district, one of the oldest villages in eastern Arunachal Pradesh, whose name means 'golden temple'. It lies near the better-known Golden Pagoda of Namsai and is a centre of Theravada Buddhist life in the region.
